opening.argument: The video presents a Lowe's-related promotion as an ordinary deal: viewers are told to text a keyword, with the required word depending on location, to access an in-store discount or a gift card worth $5 to $500. The speaker describes the offer as time-limited and encourages viewers to use it for free tissue. That framing is consistent with routine rewards and promotional deal-sharing; there is no discussion of investing, collection of credentials, or a demonstrated deceptive mechanism. The stated savings and Lowe's control of the short code or website are not verified, so the offer should not be treated as confirmed. But those limits do not change what the video actually shows: a retail promotion, not evidence of a scam.

citations.quote: I wanted to share with you all a deal at Lowe's going on.
So if you have time, go out there, you can get some free tissue.
